deployment.name: Winter Field Day 2027
deployment.description: Annual cold-weather field exercise. DeKalb ARES operates WD5EMA as class 2O (two transmitters, outdoor) from the Stone Mountain Park campground: one HF station, one VHF/UHF station, a digital position and a Winlink gateway, all on battery and solar. Operating period 1600 UTC Saturday 30 January to 2159 UTC Sunday 31 January 2027 (11:00 Saturday to 16:59 Sunday local). Rovers test simplex and 40 m VarAC into the site.
deployment.tasking_reference: Winter Field Day 2027 rules; club call WD5EMA, class 2O, section GA

sites.name: Stone Mountain Park campground, group site
sites.address: 4003 Stonewall Jackson Dr, Stone Mountain, GA 30083
sites.parking_notes: Park entry fee or annual pass at the gate. Park on the gravel pad next to the group site; keep the loop road clear for the campground host.
sites.arrival_notes: Enter by the East Gate off US-78 (exit 8), follow the campground signs, then the loop to the group site. Setup starts 08:00 Saturday; operating starts 11:00 sharp.
sites.access_notes: Campground gate closes at 22:00; get the code from the station captain if you arrive later. Cell coverage is one to two bars; the site has no grid power by design.

sites.name: Backup site: DeKalb Fire HQ and EOC parking lot
sites.arrival_notes: Used only if the park closes for weather. The move decision is made by 18:00 Friday and pushed to every packet.
sites.access_notes: Simplex from this lot to Stone Mountain failed at 50 W in the 2026 drill: plan on the repeater for talk-in.

categories.name: Safety
categories.description: Safety officer checks these on arrival

items.name: Second HF transceiver for the digital position
Multiband HF wire antenna and push-up mast
2 m Yagi and 6 m loop with rotator or armstrong mount
Logging laptops with N1MM Logger+ networked
items.description: One per station plus the captain

items.name: Solar panels 200 W with charge controller
Coffee, hot water, food plan for 24 hours
First aid kit and fire extinguisher

tasks.name: Reserve the campground group site
tasks.description: Confirm the reservation and the gate code

tasks.name: Go or no-go weather call
tasks.description: Decide by 18:00 Friday; publish the plan so every packet updates

tasks.name: Print the bulletin schedule and band plan
Submit the log before 1 March
tasks.description: ADIF from N1MM, objectives ticked, bulletin text pasted

tasks.name: Confirm the backup site with DEMA
tasks.description: Parking lot access and EOC restroom

positions.name: Station captain and logging (N1MM)
positions.briefing_notes: Runs the site: band plan, operator rotation, N1MM network, ADIF export and the log submission before 1 March. Holds the campground gate code. Signs off objectives as they are met.

positions.name: HF station

requirements.notes: Technicians operate under the control operator at the station

positions.briefing_notes: Two operators per shift: one on the mic, one logging and spotting. Work 80, 40, 20, 15 and 10 m as the bands open; three QSOs on each band is objective 3. Exchange: WD5EMA 2O GA.

positions.name: VHF/UHF station
positions.briefing_notes: 2 m Yagi on the push-up mast and the 6 m loop. FM simplex and SSB; talk the rovers in on 146.550 and log them as QSOs.

positions.name: Digital position (VarAC, JS8Call)
positions.briefing_notes: Shares the HF antenna by schedule with WFD HF (agree the band plan with the captain). 40 m VarAC on 7.105 USB for the rovers; JS8Call for the digital objective. WSJT modes do not count for WFD.

positions.name: Winlink gateway

requirements.notes: Starlink or hotspot for the CMS link

positions.briefing_notes: Bring up the VARA FM gateway on 145.070 with CMS access over Starlink. Second objective: a local Winlink post office so the stations can pass messages when the internet is down.

positions.name: Safety officer

requirements.value: Completed the WFD safety checklist last year or ARRL FD safety officer role

positions.briefing_notes: Walk the site before operating starts: guy lines flagged, feedline off walkways, heater ventilation, fuel stored away from tents, first aid kit located, weather watched. Sign the safety checklist in the app before 11:00.

positions.name: Setup crew
positions.briefing_notes: Antennas, shelters, power and tables up by 10:30 so the stations can test before 11:00.

positions.name: Teardown crew
positions.briefing_notes: From 17:00 Sunday: strike antennas first while there is light, then shelters. Check the asset list before leaving.

positions.name: Rover 1
positions.briefing_notes: Drive to three locations of your choice, send an APRS message to WD5EMA with your location, then work the site on 146.550 simplex and, if you have HF, 40 m VarAC. Report which locations worked for the coverage map.

positions.name: Rover 2
positions.briefing_notes: Same brief as Rover 1; coordinate locations so you do not overlap.

shifts.notes: Gateway up before 11:00; may leave it running unattended overnight.

channels.name: Simplex 146.550
channels.remarks: Repeaters-down fallback and for taking a conversation off the net.

channels.name: RACE net repeater (W4DOC 146.820)
channels.remarks: Atlanta Radio Club. Aid stations, shadows, pace cars.

channels.name: APRS 144.390 (RF)
channels.remarks: Rovers spot themselves by APRS message to WD5EMA. Works from most of DeKalb; downtown Atlanta does not.

channels.name: 40 m VarAC 7.105 USB
channels.remarks: VarAC calling frequency for the rovers. Dial 7.105 USB.

channels.name: WD5EMA Winlink gateway (VARA FM 145.070)
channels.remarks: Field gateway with CMS access over Starlink; local post office when the internet is down.

channels.name: Station captain mobile phone
channels.remarks: One or two bars at the campground. Replace with the captain's number.

comms_plans.name: WFD 2027 communications plan
comms_plans.special_instructions: Talk-in on 146.550 simplex from 08:00 Saturday. If you cannot raise the site on simplex, call on the W4DOC repeater. Rovers announce each location by APRS message before calling on voice.

rows.remarks: Monitor at WFD VHF all weekend.
Also the backup-site link if we move.
APRS message to WD5EMA with your location.
40 m VarAC when 2 m does not reach.
Send a Winlink check-in from home before you drive out.
Weak signal at the site; text first.
Repeater down: relay through Rover 1 from the top of the mountain road.

objectives.title: Field station on the air for 6 continuous hours
objectives.description: Class 2O WD5EMA from the campground: HF and VHF transmitters, multiband HF antenna, 2 m Yagi and 6 m loop. Technicians get HF time under the control operator.

objectives.title: Shelters up for comfortable operating
objectives.description: Canopies with sidewalls, heater with ventilation, tables and lighting before 11:00.

objectives.title: Three QSOs on each of six bands
objectives.description: 80, 40, 20, 15, 10 and 2 m. Track per band on the whiteboard.

objectives.title: Every QSO logged in N1MM and exported as ADIF
objectives.description: One networked log; captain exports and submits before 1 March.

objectives.title: Three modes worked: SSB, FM and digital
objectives.description: JS8Call or VarAC count; WSJT modes do not.

objectives.title: 100 percent battery and solar, no grid power
objectives.description: Radios, laptops and lights. Log the power source for the objective multiplier.

objectives.title: QSOs from more than one HF antenna and one VHF/UHF antenna
objectives.description: Multiband wire plus a vertical; Yagi plus the loop.

objectives.title: Winlink gateway with CMS access
objectives.description: VARA FM on 145.070 over Starlink; send one message from each station through it.

objectives.title: Copy the WFD special bulletin
objectives.description: SSB, CW or digital per the bulletin schedule; paste the text into the log submission.

objectives.title: Satellite QSO
objectives.description: FM or SSB/digital pass; multiplier only, not QSO points.

objectives.title: Local Winlink post office
objectives.description: Post office linked to the gateway; send and receive between stations with the internet unplugged.

objectives.title: Rover check-ins from three locations
objectives.description: Each rover: APRS message, then 2 m simplex or 40 m VarAC into the site. Log which locations worked.

safety_checklist.template_name: ARRL Field Day safety check list

items.text: Fuel for generators stored properly and safely away from operating positions
Fire extinguisher on hand and readily available at each generator and operating position
First aid kit on hand and its location known to everyone on site
Access to NWS or other weather information; a plan for severe weather
Tent stakes, guy lines and cables flagged; trip hazards marked or covered
Electrical wiring safe: GFCI protection, properly rated extension cords, no exposed connections
Generators properly grounded; exhaust away from people, tents and openings
All antenna supports and towers erected with adequate help and clear of power lines
Antenna structures, masts and guys checked before use and after weather changes
RF exposure evaluated; feedlines and antennas kept out of reach where power justifies it
Fuel, gas cylinders and generators kept away from open flames and smoking
Site access and lighting adequate for arrivals and departures after dark
Adequate water, shade and rest arrangements for the expected weather
Minors supervised by an adult at all times; visitors briefed on hazards
Emergency contacts, nearest hospital and site address posted at the operating positions
Safety briefing delivered to every operator on arrival
